summary: Flags comments whose first alphabetic character after leading whitespace/punctuation is lowercase when 'always' is configured.
fixDescription: Capitalizes the first alphabetic character in the comment text after any leading whitespace or comment markers, preserving all other characters and whitespace exactly.
hazards: Changing '// @ts-ignore' to '// @Ts-ignore' alters the directive meaning for TypeScript compiler, potentially enabling type checking where it was suppressed.
Modifying '/* global foo */' to '/* Global foo */' breaks ESLint's special global directive parsing, causing the global declaration to be ignored.
Uppercasing '// eslint-disable-next-line' to '// Eslint-Disable-Next-Line' disables the directive, allowing lint errors on the next line to be reported again.
Transforming '// http://example.com' to '// Http://example.com' changes the URL case, which may break case-sensitive links or references in documentation.
Converting '// ¡hola!' to '// ¡Hola!' modifies the initial inverted exclamation mark's linguistic context in Spanish, altering the intended tone or meaning.
Capitalizing '// 😀 emoji' to '// 😀 Emoji' shifts focus from the emoji to the following word, potentially changing the comment's emphasis or intent in informal contexts.
Editing '// _private' to '// _Private' implies a different naming convention for internal variables, misleading readers about encapsulation intent.
Altering '// TODO: fix' to '// TODO: Fix' changes the casing of a conventional task label, which might break tooling that scans for exact 'TODO' patterns.
